statement: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3 with gcd(D)=1 for which there exist an integer B>=2 and a nonempty finite set A of positive integers such that R={B^a:a in A} is contained in D, sigma(R)=sum_{d in R}1/(d-1)>=1/2, V=D minus R has min V>=4 and sigma(V)>1, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k admit an integer N(D,k,F) such that every integer n>=N is a sum of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once and coincident numerical values from different pairs retained separately.
novelty: The exact statement, all twelve dated cash-out query attempts, returned hits, primary-source checks and explicit access/relevance limitations are recorded in units/1/novelty.md, supplementing study/problem.md, study/QUERY_LOG.md and the unchanged root novelty.md.
